mechanism_narrative: The four-week mean of RETAIL_REC is -28.0 but the most recent week improved by 4.0 points to -26.4 after two flat weeks near -30, so the depressed four-week base mechanically lowers the comparison bar and retail trips continue to revert upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC moved from -30.4 at t-1w to -26.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to -28.0, i.e. no improvement relative to the last four weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES falls monotonically from -13.7 to -32.7 while RESIDENTIAL rises monotonically from 13.7 to 18.1, meaning the workforce is durably relocated into the home; the resulting loss of commuter and lunchtime footfall suppresses weekday retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days averages above -28.0 while WORKPLACES stays below -30 and RESIDENTIAL stays above 17.

failure_condition: In the next 7 days RETAIL_REC rises above -24.0 while PARKS stays above -10 and TRANSIT stays below -34.

failure_condition: TRANSIT improves by more than 8 points within two weeks while the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC stays below -28.0.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -22.0 in the next 7 days while GROCERY_PHARM stays at or above 0.0.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages above -26.4 over the next 14 days while WORKPLACES remains below -30.

mechanism_narrative: Conditional on an early-reopening regime where GROCERY_PHARM is non-negative and PARKS is above -10, the constraint set has loosened enough that retail trips resume: GROCERY_PHARM at 0.4 and PARKS at -5.9 jointly precede a rise in RETAIL_REC above its -28.0 four-week mean within four weeks.
